oneOf.description: Owner-reviewed application boundary for reusable native UI operations.

application.description:
Device-issued reference to an observed object. Desktop references follow native lifetimes.

`token` is opaque to the model and must bind the native locator,
interactive-session incarnation, adapter version, snapshot generation,
fingerprint and expiry in the device-side reference store. Native handles,
process ids, paths and coordinates are never authoritative wire inputs.

expires_at.description:
Empty for lifecycle-bound objects; RFC3339 for other object types.
This field never grants authority.

application_name.description: Resolved from an observed application by the server, never model authority.

oneOf.description: Owner-visible projection of the exact persisted command plan.

executionBasis.description:
The trust basis under which an execution draft was produced.

This is classification metadata. It is compared as part of the full draft
but deliberately excluded from the worker-field fingerprint.

oneOf.description:
Present for an interactive (PTY) command: the client opens a terminal
carrier for exactly this execution before approving.

elevated.description: The command runs `sudo`/`doas`; the owner may be asked for a password.

execRequestId.description: Server-derived execution id the carrier is prepared for.

targetConnectionId.description: Host connection the command runs on.

sandbox.description:
How the command runs: sandboxed with its writable locations, or
unrestricted with a prominent or neutral mark.

attention.description:
`sandboxed`, or for an unrestricted command `prominent` (changes
outside the snapshot directories cannot be undone) or `neutral`.

oneOf.description:
The account an unrestricted command runs as, present when it is an
administrator, SYSTEM or root.

root.description: Effective uid 0 on Linux or macOS.

items.description: Locations a sandboxed command may write besides its write roots.

implicitWritable.description:
Locations a sandboxed command may always write: its own temporary
directory and, per platform, the macOS user temporary directory or
Linux `/dev/shm`.

mode.description: How the device runs a sealed command.

items.description:
One snapshot root as the owner sees it: the `cwd` string or the approved
directory's canonical path.

kind.description: What a root is, for the approval card.

writableRoots.description:
Write roots of a sandboxed command (its snapshot directories); empty
when it may write only temporary locations or runs unrestricted.

oneOf.description:
Best-effort snapshot taken before the command runs: covered
directories, exclusions, limits and unprotected areas. Absent for a
read-only command or when there is nothing to snapshot.

estimated_file_count.description: Size of the device's latest manifest for these roots, when known.

honors_ignore_files.description: `.gitignore` and `.ignore` rules under a root are honored.

items.description:
One snapshot root as the owner sees it: the `cwd` string or the approved
directory's canonical path.

kind.description: What a root is, for the approval card.

items.description: Areas a best-effort snapshot does not detect or cannot restore.

oneOf.description:
One command restore awaiting approval. The card always warns that the list
may include changes the command did not make, including the owner's or the
AI's own edits during the execution window.

directoryRequestId.description: The directory approval, for a root from an approved directory.

items.description:
One file the restore puts back. `change` is what the command did: an added
file is deleted, a modified file gets its previous content, a deleted file
is recreated.

rootKind.description: What a root is, for the approval card.

rootPath.description: The command's working directory, for a working-directory root.

sourceResultCallId.description: Result whose recorded changes are undone.

oneOf.description:
Safe owner-facing projection of a frozen exact-send request. Browser
references, canonical permission JSON, credentials, and pairing secrets are
deliberately excluded.
Owner-visible native launch identity; no opaque approval token is exposed.

One exact text change awaiting approval. An update carries either `edits`
or `write`; a restore carries `restore`; a deletion carries neither.

items.description: One exact edit, matched in the result of the edits before it.

replace_all.description: Replace every non-overlapping match; otherwise exactly one must match.

edits.description: Exact edits, applied in order to the result of the previous edit.

expectedSha256.description: Version an update or deletion requires.

operation.description:
Device facts, not authorization. A recovery location must be retained even
when a mutation crossed the commit point but could not be verified.

recoverable.description: The device keeps the previous state; the change can be restored.

backupCreatedAtUnixMs.description: When the restored backup was taken.

fileExpectedToExist.description: The file must exist now (false: a deleted file is recreated).

originalOperation.description: Operation whose previous state is restored.

overridesNonAiVersion.description:
The current file is not the version that operation produced; the card
must warn that it will be overwritten.

sourceResultCallId.description:
Result the change is based on: the file version an update or deletion
requires, or the operation a restore undoes.

write.description: Complete new content of a full rewrite.

screen.description:
Exact screen geometry observed immediately before one raw-input fallback
step. The edge re-resolves the owner-selected display and foreground
application, then requires these physical-pixel and DPI facts to remain
identical before injecting anything. Coordinates are never interpreted in
a stale or model-selected display space.

key.description:
Closed navigation-key set for the raw-input beta. Arbitrary virtual-key
codes and modifier chords are deliberately absent, so this cannot become a
hidden command launcher or macro surface.

step.description:
One and only one bounded raw-input fallback step. A sealed plan containing
this action must contain exactly one action, and completion remains
unverified until a later semantic or screen observation proves the intended
application state.
